battle.name: 波斯第二次入侵希臘
battle.theater: 塞薩利、溫泉關與阿提卡
battle.brief: 480 年薛西斯一世率波斯大軍渡海峽西征，溫泉關與阿提米西姆之後，海軍敗於薩拉米斯，陸軍翌年崩於普拉提亞。卡面亞述長弓屬已亡亞述的角木筋複合弓，前 612 年經米底傳入波斯，成為波斯遠射主力，也正是全軍推進的節奏所在。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 這場戰爭是阿契美尼德王朝在薛西斯一世手上對希臘本土發動的第二次大規模入侵，前鋒於公元前 480 年春渡過赫勒斯滂特海峽，主戰延續到 479 年普拉提亞與米卡列兩役而告終。波斯一方並非單一民族，而是以波斯人與米底人為骨幹，糅合薩迦斯、呂底亞、俾斯提亞、阿拉伯、埃及、埃塞俄比亞、印度、腓尼基、敘利亞、卡里亞等行省與屬國提供的步兵、騎兵、舟船與輜重。指揮系統以薛西斯親率的御營為核心：王族近衛一萬名「不死軍」步兵與一千名御林騎兵貼身防衛大王，外圍是各部族按千人營編成的方陣，軍中設千夫長與五十人長，另有司糧官與測定道路的工程師。遠征的戰略縱深在薩迪斯，船舶自愛琴海、赫勒斯滂特與黑海三面集中，腓尼基人與塞浦路斯人負責架橋與操舟，希臘人則被描寫成以「休息、飽食與婦女」度日的柔弱之民。希臘一方是臨時拼成的城邦聯軍：斯巴達、雅典、科林斯、底比斯、埃維亞、克里特、安布拉西俄科斯等邦各出兵，由各邦領袖組成的戰時會議與兩名統帥交替主持；海軍聯盟由雅典人提摩斯托克利實際調度，陸軍則經過激烈爭吵才確定由斯巴達王列昂尼達斯率領。聯軍內部部署割裂：斯巴達與伯羅奔尼撒派兵守科林斯地峽，雅典與其盟友佈防薩拉米斯海峽，彼此的戰略目標從一開始就不一致，這種裂痕在薩拉米斯海戰前後被波斯人利用，也決定了戰役的形態。
countriesEn: This war was the second large-scale invasion of the Greek mainland launched by the Achaemenid dynasty under Xerxes I; the vanguard crossed the Hellespont in the spring of 480 BC and the main fighting ran on until the battles of Plataea and Mycale in 479. The Persian side was not a single people but a mixture with Persians and Medes at its core, drawing infantry, cavalry, shipping and baggage trains from the satrapies and dependencies of Sogdia, Lydia, Bactria, Arabia, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Phoenicia, Syria and Caria. The command system was centred on the royal camp led by Xerxes himself: ten thousand immortal infantry and a thousand Immortals' cavalry guarded the Great King at close quarters, while outside them stood the tribal phalanxes organised in units of a thousand, with commanders of a thousand and of fifty, plus logisticians and engineers whose task was to survey the roads. The strategic depth of the expedition lay at Sardis, from which ships converged on the Aegean, the Hellespont and the Black Sea; Phoenicians and Cypriots built the bridges and handled the ships, while the Greeks were described as a soft people who passed their time in ease, in eating and in women. The Greek side was a coalition patched together on the spot: Sparta, Athens, Corinth, Thebes, Euboea, Crete, the Ambraciots and others each supplied contingents, and control rested with a council of the leading men from the various states and with two commanders in turn. The naval league was in fact directed by the Athenian Themistocles, and the command of the army was settled only after bitter argument, in favour of the Spartan king Leonidas. The deployment of the coalition was divided from the start: Sparta and the Peloponnese posted men to guard the Isthmus of Corinth, while Athens and its allies covered the straits of Salamis, and their differing strategic aims were exploited by the Persians around the time of the battle of Salamis, and in the end determined the shape of the whole campaign.
people: 波斯的核心是薛西斯一世。他以嫉妒與權謀聞名，即位後把其兄阿爾塔克塞魯斯之死說成弒逆，藉此清除異己，並於公元前 484 年允許薩迦斯首領高墨斯率眾越過哈爾哈斯河，以摧毀米底人的抵抗；高墨斯失敗被殺之後，大批米底人被貶為奴隸，這使遠征蒙上報復的色彩。他的堂兄馬爾多尼烏斯是全軍最能幹的將領之一，率六萬人留駐色薩利，並在公元前 480 年冬進入阿提卡、焚燒雅典；他的姻親阿爾塔巴茲斯則在普拉提亞戰後率殘部由山隙突圍。希臘方面的關鍵人物是斯巴達王列昂尼達斯與雅典執政官提摩斯托克利。列昂尼達斯在公元前 480 年以三百名斯巴達重裝步兵、數百名忒斯庇亞人與其餘盟軍扼守溫泉關，據希羅多德記載他在出發前得到「要麼王宮傾覆、要麼王室城邑傾覆」的神諭，仍決定留守；受降的埃菲亞萊圖斯索要金幣不成、索槍時，列昂尼達斯扯下長矛的一截相贈。埃菲亞萊圖斯是個被主人放逐的僕人，他說服波斯人沿卡利德羅摩斯山的小徑迂迴包抄，此人的一次告密決定了溫泉關的勝負。雅典的提摩斯托克利則力主把海軍集結在薩拉米斯海峽之內，不惜假稱要封鎖地峽來說服伯羅奔尼撒聯軍，並以木樁與封閉水道的方法把波斯大軍困在狹窄海面。普拉提亞方面，斯巴達的保山尼亞斯指揮聯軍左翼，雅典的阿里斯德統率右翼一萬名重裝步兵；底比斯的阿蒙法瑞圖斯率四百名底比斯人倒向波斯陣營，在普拉提亞遭包圍後三百人戰死、百人被俘。卡里亞女王阿耳忒彌西婭自帶五艘船參戰，在薩拉米斯勸薛西斯勿攻，戰後又以麵包與酒款待希臘人，其子皮辛德利斯後來在米卡列率十艘船投向波斯。
peopleEn: The central figure on the Persian side was Xerxes I. He was known for jealousy and for his mastery of court intrigue; on taking the throne he presented the death of his brother Artaxerxes as a regicide and used it to clear out his rivals, and in 484 BC he allowed the Sogdian leader Gaumes to cross the Halys and break the Median resistance, and when Gaumes failed and was killed, a large part of the Median people was enslaved, which gave the expedition the colour of revenge. His cousin Mardonius was among the ablest commanders of the host, left with sixty thousand men in Thessaly, and entered Attica in the winter of 480 to burn Athens; his kinsman Artabazus led the survivors out through a mountain gap after Plataea. The key Greek figures were the Spartan king Leonidas and the Athenian Themistocles. Leonidas held Thermopylae in 480 with three hundred Spartan hoplites, several hundred Thespians and the rest of the allies, and Herodotus has it that before he left he received an oracle saying that either the king's house or the king's city would fall, and he stayed all the same; when Ephialtes, who had come to be bought, asked for money and then for a spear, Leonidas broke off a piece of his own spear and gave it to him. Ephialtes was a servant who had been banished by his master, and he persuaded the Persians to take the path over Mount Callidromus and outflank the pass, and one man's betrayal decided the outcome at Thermopylae. On the Athenian side Themistocles argued for keeping the fleet inside the straits of Salamis, was willing to pretend that he meant to wall the Isthmus in order to win over the Peloponnesian allies, and proposed closing the channel with stakes so that the Persian host would be trapped in narrow water. At Plataea the Spartan Pausanias commanded the left of the Greek line and the Athenian Aristides led ten thousand hoplites on the right; the Theban Amompharetus took four hundred Thebans over to the Persian side, and after being surrounded at Plataea three hundred of them were killed and a hundred taken prisoner. The Carian queen Artemisia brought five ships of her own to the campaign, advised Xerxes against attacking at Salamis, and afterwards entertained the Greeks with bread and wine; her son Pisindelis later joined the Persians with ten ships at Mycale.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長弓是古代近東的角木筋複合弓：弓臂以木為芯，內貼牛角、外包牛筋，三種材料各司其長，角負責韌性與抗裂，筋負責回彈與蓄力，木負責成形。它的形制可從亞述尼尼微的浮雕直接看見，亞述巴尼拔獅獵圖與宮殿守衛浮雕中的弓手，右手拉弦時前臂與弓身同時下壓，箭桿長而箭鏃寬大，屬於近東與伊朗弓箭的同一族群。公元前 612 年亞述被米底與巴比倫聯軍攻滅，國家雖亡，技術未失，複合弓經米底傳入波斯，到公元前 480 年已是波斯軍隊的基本武器，騎兵用弓，步兵亦用弓。希羅多德《歷史》第七卷描述薛西斯大軍的裝備：波斯人用短弓，箭桿粗大，一箭可貫數人；左手持藤編或柳條的圓盾，腰佩斧與短矛，著軟布或魚鱗甲，甲下襯以麻布的束腰戰袍。卡面「弓兵在車上射」的細節同樣切合：薛西斯大軍的方陣最前排是各部族的戰車（希羅多德記為每族各出數百至一千輛），但波斯人作戰時不把戰車投入衝鋒，只在陣前陳列，載運貴族與傳令，掩護其後的步弓箭手線。希臘一方是重裝步兵的裝備：圓盾、長矛、短劍、青銅胸甲與脛甲，配青銅或皮製頭盔；弓箭手只佔輔助，射程遠不及波斯弓，其真實用途是騷擾與掩護。希臘的決定性裝備在海上：三百餘艘三列槳戰船，每船約有一百七十名槳手，裝有撞角，可攻可守，海峽作戰時另以木樁與石塊封閉水道。攻城方面，希臘聯軍在普拉提亞外挖掘環溝、修築土壘與投石機，把波斯營地封成堡壘；波斯工程師則在赫勒斯滂特上架設浮橋，把陸軍與車隊直接送過海峽，並以海運船隊從薩迪斯輸送糧秣。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card is the composite bow of the ancient Near East, built of horn, wood and sinew: a wooden core faced on the inside with horn and wrapped on the outside with sinew, each material doing one job, horn giving toughness and resistance to splitting, sinew the snap and the stored power, wood the curve of the limb. Its shape can be read directly from the Assyrian reliefs, in the lion hunt of Ashurbanipal and in the palace guard scenes at Nineveh, where the archer's forearm and the bow descend together as the right hand draws, with long shafts and broad heads, belonging to the same family of Near Eastern and Iranian bows. In 612 BC Assyria was destroyed by a coalition of Medes and Babylonians; the state perished but the technique did not, for the composite bow passed to the Persians through the Medes, and by 480 BC it was the basic weapon of the Persian army, used by the cavalry and by the infantry alike. Herodotus describes the equipment of Xerxes' host in the seventh book: the Persians carried a short bow, a heavy shaft, and one arrow that could pass through several men; on the left arm they held a round shield of wicker or withies, at the belt an axe and a short spear, and they wore soft cloth or scale armour with a linen corselet beneath. The detail on the card, that the archers shot from chariots, fits as well: the front of Xerxes' array was formed by the war chariots of the tribes, Herodotus recording several hundred to a thousand from each, but the Persians did not drive them into the charge, keeping them in the line to carry nobles and messengers and to shelter the line of bowmen behind. The Greek side fought as hoplites: round shield, long spear, short sword, bronze cuirass and greaves, with bronze or leather helmets; archers were auxiliaries only, their range far shorter than the Persian bow, and their real use was to harry and to screen. The decisive Greek equipment lay at sea: a little over three hundred triremes, each with roughly one hundred and seventy oarsmen, armed with a ram, able to attack and to hold, while in the straits the Greeks added stakes and blocks of stone to close the channel. For siege work the Hellenic allies dug a trench and raised earthworks and stone-throwers around the Persian camp at Plataea, turning it into a fortress; the Persian engineers spanned the Hellespont with pontoon bridges that carried the army and its wagons straight across, and grain came to them by sea from Sardis.
tactics: 波斯方的戰術大綱是三路並進、海陸齊頭：陸軍自小亞細亞經色雷斯的數條道路北上，海軍沿愛琴海南下，約在赫勒斯滂特與特洛伊一帶會合；浮橋與糧秣船保證了遠在大陸腹地的薩迪斯能夠持續供應這支龐大隊伍。渡海峽之後，波斯沒有急於求戰，而是以騎兵偵察、迫希臘聯軍集結，再依「以弓箭消耗、以騎兵衝擊」的公式推進。溫泉關一役，波斯軍雖多，但被地形壓縮成狹窄通道，弓箭手的拋射面被山壁切斷，無法展開人數優勢；希臘聯軍以槍盾抵牆，用長矛刺穿被逼到牆下的波斯人，用不足七千人守住了唯一可通行的山口。真正的轉折在海上：提摩斯托克利力主把希臘艦隊封在薩拉米斯海峽之內，波斯海軍的龐大船身在狹窄水道中無法展開，尾部不斷被希臘船的撞角攻擊；薛西斯本人在岸上觀戰，見旗幟與傳令失序而失去對全軍的控制，最終下令撤退，殘餘艦隊退入島嶼與本土之間的開放水域，聯軍則得以保住主力。陸軍方面，馬爾多尼烏斯在阿提卡焚燒雅典後仍留駐色薩利，未能在冬季前趕到前線，這使波斯軍在希臘南部過冬，而希臘聯軍得以在普拉提亞完成合圍：聯軍在城北挖溝築壘，把三十萬人的營地封成一個巨大堡壘，只留東面靠山的一個出口，並派一萬人駐守；同時以三路夜行軍翻越基泰戎山的三個隘口，在波斯軍側後展開攻擊。普拉提亞的會戰因此不是雙方在平原上的對撞，而是圍城、封鎖、夜襲與野戰的合奏。戰役之後，波斯殘部退往米卡列，希臘聯軍以八十艘戰艦在該處登陸作戰，把海戰與陸戰合為一役，摧毀了尚存的波斯艦隊。
tacticsEn: The Persian plan of battle was threefold advance with sea and land moving together: the army came north from Asia Minor by several roads through Thrace while the fleet worked down the Aegean, the two joining around the Hellespont and Troy, and the pontoon bridges and the grain ships allowed Sardis, far inland in the Asian continent, to keep feeding this enormous force. After the crossing Xerxes did not hurry to give battle: he scouted with cavalry, forced the Hellenic coalition to concentrate, and then advanced on the formula of exhausting the enemy with arrows and breaking him with cavalry. At Thermopylae the Persian numbers counted for little, because the ground compressed them into a narrow defile and the bowmen's arc of fire was cut off by the cliffs, so that their numbers could not be deployed; the Greeks set their spears and shields against the wall of the pass and ran down the men who were forced against it, holding the one practicable route with fewer than seven thousand men. The real turning point came at sea. Themistocles pressed for the Greek fleet to be shut inside the straits of Salamis; the huge Persian hulls could not deploy in narrow water and their sterns were repeatedly struck by the Greek rams. Xerxes watched from the shore, lost control of the host when the signals and the messengers fell out of order, and finally ordered the retreat, the surviving ships falling back into the open water between the island and the mainland, and so the coalition was able to save its main force. On land, Mardonius burned Athens and then still sat in Thessaly, failing to reach the front before winter, which left the Persian army in southern Greece over the winter and gave the Hellenic allies time to complete their encirclement at Plataea: north of the town they dug a trench and raised earthworks, sealing the camp of three hundred thousand men into a vast fortress with a single exit on the mountain side to the east, and a force of ten thousand was posted to watch it. At the same time the allies marched by night in three columns over the three passes of Mount Cithaeron and came out on the flank of the Persian position. The battle of Plataea was therefore not a head-on collision on open ground but a compound of investment, blockade, night movement and field combat. After it the Persian remnants withdrew towards Mycale, where the Hellenic fleet of eighty ships landed men and fought ashore, joining a sea battle and a land battle into one action and destroying the last Persian ships.
data: 有根據的數字不多，能核對者如下。希羅多德《歷史》第七卷把薛西斯遠征軍的總數記為步兵五百十七萬、騎兵一百五十萬、戰艦一千二百零七艘，另記渡海峽的開支達三百萬；歷代學者多視之為夸張，通常認為實際規模在數十萬量級，可能夸大一至兩個數量級。希臘聯軍的總數，他記為步兵約三十萬、騎兵八千；出現在阿提米西姆海面的希臘戰船為二百七十一艘。溫泉關狹隘內實際作戰的聯軍，計有斯巴達三百人、忒斯庇亞人七百、底比斯人四百、梅加拉人一千、赫利亞人五百以及其餘盟軍兵，合計約七千人；波斯方面的損失，希羅多德按其民族分列統計，概括數字常被引作四萬，斯巴達的傳令官斐尼克斯則報稱波斯軍死一千。希羅多德記希臘軍在阿提米西姆的三日海戰中損失四十艘戰船，波斯軍損失二百艘；薩拉米斯海戰他記希臘軍失四十艘、波斯軍失二百艘，即波斯海軍折損約六分之一。波斯大軍渡海峽時架設兩座浮橋，一座供步兵與車隊、一座供騎兵，橋面總長約兩公里上下。希臘聯軍在普拉提亞外修築的環形工事，圍長約十二公里，即古代一日行程，修築用了一日半。普拉提亞會戰，聯軍投入約八萬步兵與八千騎兵，波斯方面記為三十萬步兵、一千騎兵；波斯軍死亡約四萬人，聯軍陣亡約一千人。普拉提亞戰後，阿爾塔巴茲斯率六萬人由山隙逃出，阿里斯莫多圖斯所部三萬人則被全殲，四百名底比斯人中三百人戰死、百人被俘。薛西斯退回亞洲時帶走的是大軍中的一部分。希羅多德另記兩次日食：薩拉米斯海戰之前一次（後世推算為公元前 480 年 9 月 2 日），普拉提亞之戰當日一次（後世推算為公元前 479 年 9 月 30 日），他以為那是大軍覆沒的凶兆。
dataEn: The number of figures that can be checked is not large, and only those are listed here. In the seventh book of the Histories Herodotus gives the total of Xerxes' invading force as 5,170,000 foot, 1,500,000 horse and 1,207 warships, and he records the cost of the crossing at three hundred talents; generations of scholars have regarded these as inflated, and the real size is usually put in the hundreds of thousands, perhaps exaggerated by one or two orders of magnitude. He gives the total of the Hellenic force as about 300,000 foot and 8,000 horse, and the number of Greek ships present at Artemisium as 271. The allies who actually fought in the narrow pass at Thermopylae numbered some seven thousand: three hundred Spartans, seven hundred Thespians, four hundred Thebans, a thousand Megarians, five hundred Helians and the rest of the contingents. For Persian losses Herodotus itemises them by people, and the figure usually quoted in summary is forty thousand, while the Spartan herald Phoenix reported a thousand Persian dead. Herodotus records that the Greeks lost forty ships in the three-day sea fight at Artemisium and the Persians two hundred, and that at Salamis the Greeks lost forty and the Persians two hundred, that is, about a sixth of the Persian fleet. Two pontoon bridges were built for the crossing of the Hellespont, one for the infantry and wagons and one for the cavalry, with a total deck length of roughly two kilometres. The circumvallation the Hellenic allies raised outside Plataea was about twelve kilometres round, a day's journey of the ancient world, and took a day and a half to build. At the battle of Plataea the allies put in about 80,000 foot and 8,000 horse against a Persian force recorded as 300,000 foot and 1,000 horse; about forty thousand Persians were killed and about a thousand of the Greeks. After Plataea Artabazus led sixty thousand men out through the mountain gap, while the thirty thousand of Arismodotus were destroyed and three hundred of the four hundred Thebans were killed with a hundred taken prisoner. Only a part of the host was carried back to Asia by Xerxes. Herodotus also records two solar eclipses, one before the battle of Salamis, which modern computation dates to 2 September 480 BC, and one on the day of the battle of Plataea, dated to 30 September 479 BC; he took them as omens of the destruction of the great host.
cause: 根本的起因是波斯帝國與希臘城邦世界在四十年間的兩次正面碰撞。公元前 546 年居魯士滅米底，波斯崛起於安那托利亞東部；公元前 499 年愛奧尼亞城邦起義，波斯王宮在米利都的薩迪斯被焚，起義雖被平定，卻證明愛琴海東岸不願接受王權。公元前 490 年大流士一世派兵渡海，在馬拉松擊敗雅典，但雅典的民主改革與帝國在愛奧尼亞的治理方式並不兼容。薛西斯即位後先平定宮廷，公元前 484 年又允許高墨斯越過哈爾哈斯河摧毀米底勢力，高墨斯失敗後大批米底人被貶為奴隸，這既加深了米底與波斯貴族之間的裂痕，也讓遠征帶上報復的色彩。遠征的直接理由有三層：一是為馬拉松復仇並懲罰背叛的希臘城邦；二是薛西斯需要一場決定性的勝利來鞏固自己在宮廷中的地位；三是王位繼承的陰影，他的父親大流士正是在一次宮變中被近衛所殺，他對宮廷與近衛的戒心，部分轉化為對阿契美尼德家系能否延續的憂慮。希臘聯軍未能全力抵抗的原因也在這裡：三十餘個城邦彼此猜忌，沒有共同的法律、貨幣與長期的同盟經驗，雅典與斯巴達互不信任，誰都怕對方利用戰爭爭取霸權。因此遠征軍一路未遇強阻便連下比奧夏、菲里基等城，逐漸深入，最終在溫泉關與薩拉米斯兩處被希臘人頂住。
causeEn: The root cause lies in two head-on collisions between the Persian empire and the world of the Greek city-states within forty years. In 546 BC Cyrus destroyed Media and Persia rose in eastern Anatolia; in 499 BC the Ionian cities revolted and the Persian court at Sardis in Miletus was burned, and although the revolt was suppressed it had proved that the eastern shore of the Aegean would not accept kingship. In 490 BC Darius I sent troops across the sea and beat the Athenians at Marathon, but the democratic reform of Athens and the way the empire governed Ionia were not compatible. After taking the throne Xerxes first settled the court, and in 484 BC allowed Gaumes to cross the Halys and break the Median power; when Gaumes failed, a great part of the Medes were reduced to slavery, which deepened the rift between the Medes and the Persian nobility and gave the expedition the colour of revenge. There were three layers of immediate reason for the campaign: first, to avenge Marathon and punish the Greek states that had rebelled; second, Xerxes needed a decisive victory to confirm his position at court; and third, the shadow of the succession, for his father Darius had been killed in a palace coup by his own guards, and the ruler's distrust of the court and the guard was in part a fear for whether the Achaemenid house would endure. The reason the Hellenic coalition could not oppose the invasion in force lies in the same place: more than thirty city-states distrusted one another, with no common law, no common coinage and no long habit of alliance, and Athens and Sparta did not trust each other, each fearing that the other would use the war to win hegemony. The invading army therefore took city after city without meeting real resistance, taking Biotia and Phocis, pushing deeper into the country, and was finally halted by the Greeks at two places, Thermopylae and Salamis.
impact: 對波斯帝國，這場戰爭是阿契美尼德王朝唯一一次深度西征的失敗。薛西斯回到薩迪斯時帶回的部隊不足出徵時的一半，亞述以東的邊境重新回到米底與波斯貴族的拉鋸之中；希臘人的抵抗也讓波斯遠征的模式被重新界定，從此阿契美尼德王朝的西進重心轉向地中海東岸與埃及，波斯在希臘本土不再嘗試大規模登陸。對希臘，結果是城邦體制的延續與雅典海上帝國的興起：普拉提亞與米卡列的勝利讓戰時聯盟得以解散並重建為提洛同盟，希臘戰爭的共同體驗成為古典時期的政治記憶，斯巴達與雅典先後稱霸，經過伯羅奔尼撒戰爭與馬其頓崛起，最終走向亞歷山大大帝的東征。文化上的痕跡更深：溫泉關的三百名斯巴達重裝步兵在歐洲記憶中成為自由與視死如歸的原型，列昂尼達斯成為文學與藝術中反覆出現的形象；波斯人用弓箭射程壓倒希臘步兵的觀感，長期影響歐洲對東方的想像，也讓希臘的城邦民主與公民身份敘事獲得一個清晰的對照面。經濟上，波斯的進攻切斷了愛琴海東岸與黑海之間的小麥貿易，希臘的穀物來源被迫轉向黑海，後來雅典興建長牆與開闢黑海航線的戰略邏輯，部分即由此役而定。反過來說，希臘並未因取勝而付出代價：波斯主力沒有被包圍殲滅，希臘本土的戰鬥雖然慘烈，多數城邦的城牆與農田卻得以保存，而同一時期的小亞細亞行省與兩河流域則長期承受徵斂、役使與反亂。
impactEn: For the Persian empire this war was the failure of the only deep westward expedition the Achaemenid dynasty ever attempted. The troops Xerxes brought back to Sardis were fewer than half of those he had taken out, and the frontier east of Assyria returned to the tug of war between Medes and Persian nobles. Greek resistance also redefined the Persian mode of conquest: from then on the Achaemenid turn of expansion lay in the eastern Mediterranean and in Egypt, and Persia never again attempted a large landing in mainland Greece. For Greece the result was the survival of the city-state system and the rise of the Athenian maritime empire. The victories of Plataea and Mycale allowed the wartime coalition to dissolve and be rebuilt as the Delian League, and the shared memory of the Persian war became a political inheritance of the classical age: Sparta and Athens in turn held hegemony, and after the Peloponnesian War and the rise of Macedon the road ran on to the expedition of Alexander. The cultural marks run deeper still. The three hundred Spartan hoplites at Thermopylae became in European memory the type of freedom and of dying fearlessly, and Leonidas remains a figure who returns again and again in literature and in art. The sense that the Persians beat Greek infantry with the reach of the bow shaped Europe's long imagining of the East and gave the Greek narrative of democracy and citizenship a clear foil. Economically, the Persian attack cut the grain trade between the eastern Aegean and the Black Sea and forced Greek grain sources towards the Black Sea, so that part of the strategic logic behind the later Athenian long walls and the Black Sea grain route grew out of this campaign. And Greece did not pay a heavy price for the victory: the Persian main force was not surrounded and destroyed, and although the fighting on Greek soil was bitter, the walls and fields of most cities survived, while in the same years the satrapies of Asia Minor and the Mesopotamian river valleys bore conscription, corvée and revolt.
result: 從軍事結果看，波斯第二次入侵希臘以失敗告終，失敗方式也很清楚：海上的損失在薩拉米斯，陸上骨幹在普拉提亞。薛西斯本人在薩拉米斯戰敗後退回小亞細亞，把殘餘陸軍交給馬爾多尼烏斯指揮，自己仍留在海峽對岸觀望，直到馬爾多尼烏斯敗亡才返回薩迪斯。馬爾多尼烏斯於公元前 480 年冬率六萬人屯於色薩利，翌年在普拉提亞被聯軍包圍並全軍覆沒，他本人陣亡，屍首未能尋回；亞軍殘部在阿爾塔巴茲斯率領下由山隙逃出，損失慘重。追擊在米卡列的海灘上完成，希臘聯軍登陸作戰，波斯殘餘艦隊被摧毀，希臘聯軍隨後圍困普拉提亞城，迫使馬爾多尼烏斯留下的守軍投降。戰果的歸屬在兩戰之間定下：斯巴達得到陸上首功，雅典得到海上主導權，這一分配日後演成兩強對抗，最終在伯羅奔尼撒戰爭中爆發，希臘的地中海霸權則在羅馬手中終結。戰後的希臘沒有進一步追擊波斯本土，聯盟在提洛島設立後轉向維持海上秩序，把同盟的貢金集中到提洛島，用這些錢建立雅典的城牆與海軍，形成延續數百年的海上帝國；公元前 478 年提洛同盟正式成立，公元前 466 年埃烏律墨得河一役又清剿了波斯在愛琴海東岸的殘餘勢力。波斯方面在薛西斯於公元前 465 年去世後迎來又一次宮廷變亂，其後阿契美尼德王朝的注意力轉向亞洲腹地與埃及，與希臘的衝突被凍結在小亞細亞的附庸治理與愛琴海的自治這一形式裡：波斯守住亞洲，希臘守住海洋，這個均衡維持了數百年。
resultEn: Militarily the second Persian invasion of Greece ended in failure, and the manner of that failure is clear: the loss at sea came at Salamis, the loss of the army's backbone came at Plataea. After the defeat at Salamis Xerxes withdrew to Asia Minor, handing the remnant of the land army to Mardonius to command, and remained himself on the far side of the strait to watch, returning to Sardis only after Mardonius was defeated. Mardonius wintered with sixty thousand men in Thessaly in 480 BC and in the following year was encircled by the allies at Plataea and destroyed with his whole army; he was killed there and his body was never recovered, while the remaining sixty thousand under Artabazus escaped through the mountain gap at heavy cost. The pursuit was completed on the shore of Mycale, where the Hellenic allies landed and fought and the last Persian ships were destroyed; they then invested Plataea itself and forced Mardonius' garrison to surrender. The division of the spoils was settled between the two battles: Sparta took the credit on land and Athens took the command at sea, and that division later hardened into the rivalry between the two powers which erupted in the Peloponnesian War, while the Greek mastery of the Mediterranean was finally settled in the hands of Rome. Greece did not pursue the war into Persian territory. Once the league was moved to Delos it turned to policing the sea, concentrating the tribute of the allies on the island and using that money to build the walls and the navy of Athens, and so a maritime empire lasted for centuries: the Delian League was formally constituted in 478 BC, and in 466 the battle of the Eurymedon swept away the last Persian power on the eastern Aegean coast. On the Persian side, Xerxes died in 465 BC and was followed by another palace upheaval, after which the Achaemenid dynasty turned its attention to the Asian interior and to Egypt. The conflict with Greece was frozen into the form of dependent rule in Asia Minor on one side and autonomy in the Aegean on the other: Persia held Asia and Greece held the sea, and that balance lasted for centuries.
